title: managed GPU provisioner module for private VPC (ASG + Karpenter)
creator: Owen Patel
description:
Summary:
Implement a reusable Terraform module that provisions GPU node pools inside customer Private VPCs with first-class support for two provisioning models: ASG-based managed node groups (for deterministic instance lifecycle & driver control) and Karpenter-based provisioning (for bursty/spot-friendly workloads). The module must work in Redwood Private deployments and include health checks, driver installation/upgrade hooks, mixed-instance/spot fallback, and safe node upgrade strategies.

Goals:
- Single module usable by Private customers and by our internal staging clusters.
- Safe driver/OS upgrade orchestration with minimal disruption to running inference workloads.
- Explicit health checks at both instance and Kubernetes node level (kubelet, docker/CRI, NVIDIA driver, kube-proxy).
- Autoscaler integration with capacity fallback: if GPU spot capacity unavailable, fall back to smaller non-GPU nodes for low-priority workloads.
- Clear observability (node provisioning metrics, upgrade progress, failure reasons) and alerts.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Dual-mode approach (ASG vs Karpenter): ASG offers predictable lifecycle for critical customers requiring fixed node counts and driver control; Karpenter is optimized for bursty inference and cost efficiency. Creating two modes in one module increases complexity but reduces drift between our internal config and customer configs.
- Driver management: we will use a node-level systemd unit (delivered via encrypted userdata) to install NVIDIA drivers and DCGM where needed. For ASG nodes we bake a baseline AMI with driver bootstrap scripts; for Karpenter we rely on a userdata + DaemonSet fallback to ensure driver presence. This balances startup time vs reproducibility.
- Healthchecks: implement AWS EC2 status checks + SSH/SSM reachable check for instance-level; for pod/node-level we create a Kubernetes NodeCondition probe (custom) and a job that validates nvidia-smi and runs a short NV compute smoke test. Failure policies: auto-cordon/drain after configurable failure threshold, alert to SRE, and optional auto-replace (ASG) or node-termination (Karpenter).
- Upgrade strategy: phased canary for AMI/driver upgrades. For ASG: create a new launch template + rolling update with pause windows, and health hooks to verify driver + small inference eval sets. For Karpenter: use test workloads and scale-up policies to validate new user-data before migrating traffic.

Module inputs (high level):
- vpc_id, subnet_ids, security_groups
- provisioning_mode: "asg" | "karpenter"
- gpu_instance_types: list
- node_taints and node_labels
- node_pool_priority: critical | default | best_effort
- driver_channel: stable | canary
- enable_spot_fallback: true|false
- healthcheck_policy JSON blob (as string) to avoid nested types in TF registry
- monitoring_exporter: prometheus/node-exporter config

Outputs (high level):
- node_pool_id / karpenter_provisioner_name
- autoscaler_hooks / lifecycle_hook_arn (ASG)
- driver_upgrade_runbook_link

Acceptance criteria:
- Module can be instantiated in a sample private VPC (internal test env) in both ASG and Karpenter modes.
- Automated test runs reproduce a driver upgrade with <5% request error rate and automated rollback on regressions.
- Healthchecks detect and cordon failing nodes and trigger alerts within 3 minutes.
- CI validates plan/apply for common permutations (gpu-only, mixed-spot, spot-fallback enabled).

Infra & security notes:
- All userdata and driver artifacts must be pulled from signed S3 artifacts and validated with checksums.
- KMS keys from the customer's Private deployment must be used for any secrets in userdata.
- Require security review prior to GA; flagging "security_review_required" on this ticket.

Follow-ups and TBDs:
- Bake AMIs for the major GPU families we support (A10G, A100, H100) and add automated tests per-architecture.
- Integrate with Redwood Console's rollout API to visualize node upgrades and allow manual aborts.
- Add a Karpenter constraint helper module to translate our cost/policy schema into ProvisionerSpec.
